title: Long-Lang Bad Suk (Living in Peace and Harmony)
author: S. S. Majaw
description: Archery and community festival phawar on unity, friendship, and collective well-being.

khasi: Ko ri baieit ko lum ba jngum,
Ha phi ki kpa ki pynshong kur,
Ban sumar hok ia ka spah mariang,
Ban kyntiew burom ia ka jait ka kynja.
english: O beloved land, O azure mountains,
Upon you the ancestors founded the clans,
To guard faithfully the wealth of nature,
To exalt the honor of the race.

khasi: Ha ka dorbar kynmaw ia ka hok,
Wat ai kan jot ka ktien u barim,
Kamai ia ka burom da ka jingshlur,
Pynneh ia ka nam ha man ki pyntha.
english: Let not the tongue of the ancient perish,
Preserve the good name across all valleys.

cultural_context: Chanted in traditional Khasi heptasyllabic and octosyllabic cadence during archery matches and communal assemblies.

vocabulary.spah mariang: natural heritage and wealth of creation

lyrics_khasi:
Ko ri baieit ko lum ba jngum,
Ha phi ki kpa ki pynshong kur,
Ban sumar hok ia ka spah mariang,
Ban kyntiew burom ia ka jait ka kynja.
Ha ka dorbar kynmaw ia ka hok,
Wat ai kan jot ka ktien u barim,
Kamai ia ka burom da ka jingshlur,
Pynneh ia ka nam ha man ki pyntha.
lyrics_english:
O beloved land, O azure mountains,
Upon you the ancestors founded the clans,
To guard faithfully the wealth of nature,
To exalt the honor of the race.
In the council remember righteousness,
Let not the tongue of the ancient perish,
Earn honor through bravery,
Preserve the good name across all valleys.
